mainTopic: Who may be included in another's עירוב, and how much food an עירוב requires
overview: The amud opens by finishing the question of how long a child counts as 'needing his mother' for her עירוב. רב יהושע בריה דרב אידי's narrow reading of רב אסי is refuted by a ברייתא that sets the age at six. רב אסי survives because 'עד' includes six. The ברייתא is reconciled with רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש by whether the father is in town. Two ברייתות then teach that a man may make an עירוב for his minor children and כנעני servants without their knowledge, because 'their hand is like his hand.' His wife, adult children and עברי servants need their knowledge. The גמרא shows that silence counts as consent, and that making one's own עירוב is the strongest protest. A new משנה sets the עירוב food at two meals per person and records several opinions on how big those meals are. The גמרא rules like רבי מאיר, and it explains why the measures of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה and רבי שמעון are 'close to equal' by deducting the grocer's profit.

steps.title: רב יהושע limits רב אסי's ruling to a case of competing עירובין
steps.stepSummary: רב יהושע בריה דרב אידי says רב אסי's rule about a six-year-old applies only when the father set up a עירוב for him to the north and the mother set one to the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהושע, son of רב אידי, said: When רב אסי said a six-year-old goes with his mother's עירוב, he meant a case where his father made a עירוב for him to the north and his mother made one for him to the south. In that case even a six-year-old prefers to be with his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an answer that narrows רב אסי's ruling so it does not clash with the shorter age range given by רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a six-year-old no longer 'needs his mother,' so he would not automatically follow her עירוב. רב יהושע says רב אסי only meant a case where both parents actively made a עירוב for the child in opposite directions. When the child must choose, he goes with his mother, because at six he still prefers her company.

keyTerms.meaning: set up a עירוב on his behalf
he is comfortable with / he prefers

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהושע is not saying a six-year-old always follows his mother. He limits רב אסי to the special case where each parent made a separate עירוב for the child.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehoshua, son of Rav Idi, said:
When Rav Asi said his ruling,
it was, for example, where his father made an eiruv for him to the north
and his mother made one for him to the south,
for even a six-year-old, too,
prefers the company of his mother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier tension (on the previous amud) between רב אסי and the definitions of רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי seemed to say any six-year-old follows his mother's עירוב, even one she made only for herself.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אסי only meant a case where both parents made separate עירובין for the child in opposite directions.

steps.title: A ברייתא lets a child use his mother's own עירוב until six
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a child who needs his mother goes out with his mother's עירוב until age six. It says nothing about competing עירובין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection: A child who needs his mother goes out with his mother's עירוב, until age six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that challenges רב יהושע's narrow reading of רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets a young child rely on his mother's ordinary עירוב, the one she made for herself, all the way up to age six. That means no special case with two competing עירובין is needed. So רב יהושע's limitation looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a tannaitic source)
a young child who still needs his mother
may go out using his mother's עירוב

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A child who needs his mother
may go out by means of his mother's eiruv —
until the age of six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the limitation proposed in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהושע בריה דרב אידי's limitation of רב אסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows a child up to six to use his mother's ordinary עירוב without any competing עירובין. That contradicts the claim that a six-year-old follows his mother only when both parents made separate עירובין for him.

steps.title: רב יהושע's view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is a full refutation of רב יהושע בר רב אידי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב יהושע בר רב אידי. It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the outcome of the challenge: רב יהושע's limitation is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double wording 'תיובתא ... תיובתא' is the formula for a final, conclusive refutation. There is no answer to the ברייתא, so רב יהושע's reading of רב אסי is dropped.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהושע's narrow reading of רב אסי (separate north and south עירובין) is rejected by the ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר רַב אִידִי
phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rav Yehoshua bar Rav Idi.
It is indeed a conclusive refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר רַב אִידִי תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge raised in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יהושע בר רב אידי's limitation of רב אסי is refuted.

steps.title: Does the ברייתא also refute רב אסי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the same ברייתא might refute רב אסי, since 'until six' may mean a six-year-old is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is also a refutation of רב אסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the same ברייתא against רב אסי himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי said a six-year-old follows his mother's עירוב. If 'until six' in the ברייתא means 'up to but not including six,' then a six-year-old would not follow her. That would contradict רב אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: let it be a refutation of him

phrases.english: Let us say it is
a refutation of Rav Asi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same ברייתא from step 2 against a different אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling that a six-year-old goes out with his mother's עירוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reading 'until six' as excluding six would mean a six-year-old does not follow his mother, which goes against רב אסי.

steps.title: 'Until' includes the endpoint
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי can answer that 'until six' in the ברייתא includes age six.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי can say to you: 'until' means up to and including.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי by reading the word 'עד' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole question depends on whether 'עד' includes the endpoint. If 'until six' includes six, then the ברייתא matches רב אסי exactly. So רב אסי survives.

keyTerms.meaning: he can say to you (a defense on his behalf)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אסי stands: 'עד בן שש' means up to and including age six.

phrases.english: Rav Asi can say to you:
'Until' means up to and including.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the source
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Until six' includes a six-year-old, so the ברייתא supports רב אסי.

steps.title: Does the ברייתא refute רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ברייתא's age of six contradicts רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש, whose definitions of 'needs his mother' point to a younger age.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a refutation of רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests the ברייתא against רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש, who defined a 'child who needs his mother' earlier on the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their definitions imply that a child stops needing his mother at a younger age, around four or five. The ברייתא extends it all the way to six. That looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who defined a 'child who needs his mother'
אמורא who gave another definition of a 'child who needs his mother'

phrases.english: Let us say it is a refutation
of Rabbi Yannai and Reish Lakish!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same ברייתא against yet another opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש's definitions of a 'child who needs his mother'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their definitions imply an age younger than six, while the ברייתא sets the limit at six.

steps.title: It depends on whether the father is in town
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction: רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש speak of a case where the father is in town, and the ברייתא speaks of a case where he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. This case is when his father is in town. That case is when his father is not in town.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each source to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the father is in town, the child can go with him, so he stops 'needing his mother' at a younger age. That is the case of רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש. When the father is away, the child depends on his mother longer, up to age six. That is the case of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (two cases, no contradiction)

steps.whatToRemember: How long a child 'needs his mother' depends on the father. If the father is in town, the age is younger (רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש). If the father is not in town, the child follows his mother until six (the ברייתא and רב אסי).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the age limit is not a fixed number. It depends on the child's real dependence on his mother, which changes when the father is present.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where his father is in town,
that one is where his father is not in town.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ אֲבוּהִי בְּמָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's age of six contradicts the younger age implied by רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: With the father in town, the younger age applies. With the father away, the child follows his mother until six.

steps.title: First teaching: whom a person may make an עירוב for
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a person may make an עירוב for his minor children and כנעני servants even without their knowledge. For עברי servants, adult children, and his wife, he needs their knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person may make an עירוב for his minor son and daughter and for his כנעני servant and maidservant, whether they know about it or not. But he may not make an עירוב for his עברי servant and maidservant, his adult son and daughter, or his wife, unless they agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that splits a person's household into two groups. One group does not need to agree to the עירוב, and the other group does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Minor children and כנעני servants are fully tied to the head of the house, so he can set their שבת location for them. Adult children, עברי servants, and a wife are independent people, so their agreement is needed. This opens a new topic after the age discussion that just ended.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
Makes an עירוב (here, an עירוב תחומין that sets a person's שבת base)
כנעני (non-Jewish, fully owned) servants as opposed to עברי (Jewish, temporarily bound) servants

phrases.english: Our Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מְעָרֵב אָדָם עַל יְדֵי בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ הַקְּטַנִּים,
phrases.english: A person may make an eiruv on behalf of his minor son and daughter,
and on behalf of his Canaanite servant and maidservant,
whether with their knowledge or without their knowledge.
But he may not make an eiruv

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל יְדֵי עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הָעִבְרִים,
phrases.english: neither on behalf of his Hebrew servant and maidservant,
nor on behalf of his adult son and daughter,
nor on behalf of his wife,
except with their knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְעָרֵב אָדָם עַל יְדֵי בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ הַקְּטַנִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within the laws of עירוב for household members, after the age discussion ended in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Minor children and כנעני servants: an עירוב may be made for them with or without their knowledge. עברי servants, adult children, and a wife: only with their knowledge.

steps.title: Second teaching gives the reason: their hand is like his hand
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא repeats the same split and adds the reason: minor children and כנעני servants can be included without knowing, because 'their hand is like his hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: A person should not make an עירוב for his adult son and daughter, his עברי servant and maidservant, or his wife, unless they agree. But he may make an עירוב for his כנעני servant and maidservant and his minor son and daughter, whether they know or not, because their hand is like his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא with the same basic rules. The new part is that it tells us why the first group does not need to agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is 'שידן כידו', meaning their hand is like his hand. Minor children and כנעני servants are treated as an extension of the head of the house, so his act counts for them. The others have their own independent 'hand,' so he cannot decide for them without consent.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Their hand is like his hand.' They are legally an extension of him.

steps.confusionAlert: The opening 'לא יערב... אלא מדעתן' sounds negative, but it means: he may make an עירוב for them only with their consent. It does not mean he can never make one for them.

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְעָרֵב אָדָם עַל יְדֵי בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ הַגְּדוֹלִים,
phrases.english: A person may not make an eiruv on behalf of his adult son and daughter,
or on behalf of his Hebrew servant and maidservant,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל יְדֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ אֶלָּא מִדַּעְתָּן.
phrases.english: or on behalf of his wife, except with their knowledge.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְעָרֵב הוּא עַל יְדֵי עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הַכְּנַעֲנִים,
phrases.english: But he may make an eiruv on behalf of his Canaanite servant and maidservant,
and on behalf of his minor son and daughter,
whether with their knowledge or without their knowledge,
because their hand is like his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the rule of step 8 from a second ברייתא and adds the reason behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Minor children and כנעני servants can be included without their knowledge because 'their hand is like his hand.' The others need consent.

steps.title: When the master's עירוב conflicts with theirs, his wins except for the wife
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא continues: if household members made their own עירוב and the master made a different one for them, they follow the master's עירוב. The wife is the exception, because she can object.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all of them who made their own עירוב, while their master also made an עירוב for them, go by their master's עירוב. The exception is the wife, because she can object.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a new case: two different עירובין, one made by the household member and one made by the master. It rules that the master's עירוב wins for everyone except the wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though some household members need to agree before an עירוב is made for them, the ברייתא says that in a conflict they still follow the master. Only the wife can override him, since she is able to protest against his עירוב. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And all of them, meaning every household member listed
Their master, the head of the household
They go by their master's עירוב

phrases.english: And all of them who made an eiruv for themselves
while their master made an eiruv for them,
go out by means of their master's eiruv,
except for the wife,
because she is able to object.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a new case of conflicting עירובין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a conflict, household members follow the master's עירוב, except the wife, who can object.

steps.title: Why is the wife different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why only the wife can object. Adult children and עברי servants are also independent, so why can't they object too?
steps.simpleTranslation: A wife, how is she different?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the ברייתא it just quoted. This sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות put the wife together with adult children and עברי servants as people who need to consent. So it seems strange that only the wife can protest against the master's עירוב. The גמרא wants to know what makes her special.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is different?' A question asking why one case is treated differently from a similar case.

phrases.english: A wife, in what way is she different?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the exception for the wife in step 10, given the grouping in steps 8 and 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why only the wife can object to the master's עירוב, when adult children and עברי servants also need to consent.

steps.title: רבה: 'wife' includes everyone like her
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the ברייתא's word 'wife' is only an example. It means the wife and anyone in her situation, such as adult children and עברי servants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The wife, and anyone who is like her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question by widening the meaning of 'wife' in the ברייתא. It covers everyone who needs to consent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife is not unique. The ברייתא names her as an example of the whole group that needs consent, and every member of that group can object to the master's עירוב. Only minor children and כנעני servants, whose 'hand is like his hand,' must follow the master.

keyTerms.meaning: And anyone who is similar to her

steps.whatToRemember: Minor children and כנעני servants are an extension of the head of the house ('שידן כידו'), so they follow his עירוב even without knowing. A wife, adult children, and עברי servants need to consent, and according to רבה all of them can object to his עירוב.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
A wife, and all who are similar to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אִשָּׁה וְכׇל דְּדָמֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Wife' in the ברייתא is an example. It includes everyone who needs to consent (adult children, עברי servants), and all of them can object to the master's עירוב.

steps.title: Inference from 'because she can object'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא and infers that only an active objection stops the wife. If she says nothing, she goes out with her husband's עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Except for the wife, because she can object.' The reason she does not follow him is that she objected. But if she said nothing, she goes out with her husband's עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's exception for the wife and draws an inference from its wording. This inference sets up the challenges that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives the reason 'because she can object.' The גמרא reads this precisely: only an actual objection takes her out of her husband's עירוב. So if she was silent (סתמא), she is still included in his עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said' — a formula used to quote a source and then analyze it
Unspecified; she said nothing either way
She goes out (she may walk based on that עירוב)

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: Quoting the ברייתא's wife exception from Step 10

phrases.english: Except for the wife,
because she can object.
The reason is that she objected,
but if she said nothing, she goes out with her husband's עירוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: חוּץ מִן הָאִשָּׁה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיְּכוֹלָה לִמְחוֹת. טַעְמָא דְּמַחַי, הָא סְתָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the wording of the ברייתא's wife exception, which רבה already said includes adult children and עברי servants, and draws a new inference about silence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only an active objection removes the wife from her husband's עירוב. Silence leaves her included.

steps.title: Challenge from 'only with their knowledge'
steps.stepSummary: The רישא of the ברייתא says the wife needs to know. That seems to mean she must actively agree, which contradicts the idea that silence is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first part of the ברייתא teaches 'only with their knowledge.' Doesn't that mean they said 'yes'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from Step 13. It uses the first part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רישא said a man cannot make an עירוב for his wife 'except with their knowledge.' If 'knowledge' means she must actively say 'yes,' then silence would not be enough. That clashes with Step 13, which said silence keeps her in.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But it teaches' — introduces a source that seems to contradict
The first part of a source
'Is it not that…?' — suggests a reading that supports the challenge

phrases.english: But the first clause teaches:
'Only with their knowledge.'
phrases.notes: From the opening of this same ברייתא (Step 9): wife, adult children and עברי servants need their knowledge

phrases.english: Is it not that they said 'yes'?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָתָנֵי רֵישָׁא ״אֶלָּא מִדַּעְתָּם״. מַאי לָאו, דְּאָמְרִי: ״אִין״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference of Step 13 by using the רישא of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a silent wife goes out with her husband's עירוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'With their knowledge' seems to mean active consent. If so, silence is not enough.

steps.title: 'Knowledge' means they stayed silent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'with their knowledge' only means they knew and stayed silent. It is meant to exclude a case where they said 'no.'
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What does 'only with their knowledge' mean? That they stayed silent. It comes to exclude a case where they said 'no.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading 'with their knowledge' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Knowledge' does not mean she must say 'yes.' It means she knew about the עירוב and did not protest. The phrase rules out only a case where she said 'no.' So the רישא fits Step 13: silence is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: No (here both 'no, that's not right' and the refusal 'no')

steps.confusionAlert: The word לָא appears twice. The first לָא is the גמרא saying 'No, that reading is wrong.' The second is what the family members say: 'No, we don't want it.'

phrases.english: No. What does 'only with their knowledge' mean?
That they were silent.
It comes to exclude a case where they said 'no.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a phrase in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'With their knowledge' means they must actively say 'yes.'
steps.terutzMaskana: 'With their knowledge' means they knew and stayed silent. Only saying 'no' excludes them.

steps.title: Challenge from the case where they made their own עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says that when the household made their own עירוב and the master made another, the wife does not follow the master. No objection is mentioned, so it looks like a silent case where she still does not follow her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it teaches: 'All of them who made an עירוב, and their master made an עירוב for them, go out with their master's.' This case is unspecified, and still it teaches: 'except for the wife,' who does not go out with his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to Step 13, this time from the later part of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the ברייתא says nothing about the wife objecting. It seems to be a silent (סתמא) case. Yet she does not follow her husband's עירוב. That contradicts the inference that a silent wife goes out with her husband's עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Their master (the head of the household)
They go out (they rely on it to walk)

phrases.english: But it teaches: 'And all of them who made an eiruv,'
phrases.notes: The סיפא of the ברייתא, from Step 10

phrases.english: and their master made an eiruv for them,
go out with their master's.'
And this is an unspecified case,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי: חוּץ מִן הָאִשָּׁה דְּלָא נָפְקִי!
phrases.english: and it teaches: 'except for the wife,' who does not go out with his!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁעֵירְבוּ וְעֵירַב עֲלֵיהֶן רַבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 15 settled the רישא, the גמרא attacks the Step 13 inference again from the סיפא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a silent wife goes out with her husband's עירוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא shows a case with no stated objection where the wife still does not follow her husband.

steps.title: Making her own עירוב is the strongest objection
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that once they made their own עירוב, that act is the biggest objection possible. So the סיפא is not a silent case at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Since they made their own עירוב, you have no greater objection than this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge of Step 16. He shows that the סיפא really is a case of objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife did not need to say anything. By making her own עירוב in a different direction, she clearly showed she does not want her husband's. Actions count as objection, so the Step 13 rule stands: real silence includes her, but any objection, even through actions, excludes her.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the answer here

steps.whatToRemember: A wife (and others like her) follows the head of the household's עירוב unless she objects. Silence counts as agreement. Objection can come through words ('no') or through actions, like making her own עירוב.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since they made their own eiruv,
you have no greater objection than this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כֵּיוָן שֶׁעֵירְבוּ, אֵין לְךָ מִיחוּי גָּדוֹל מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 and keeps the inference of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the סיפא is not silent but an objection through action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא is a silent case, and still the wife does not follow her husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: Making her own עירוב is itself the greatest objection, so the סיפא is a case of objection.

steps.title: The basic measure: two meals per person
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה states that the food for an עירוב must be enough for two meals for each person it covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How much food does an עירוב need? Enough food for two meals for each and every person.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It tells us the size of the food used for an עירוב: two meals' worth for every person included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא discussed who is included in an עירוב. Now the משנה turns to how much food is needed. The rule is 'two meals' for each person, but it does not yet say how big a meal is. That is the next question.
steps.whyThisMatters: Everything that follows in this משנה and גמרא is an attempt to define how big these 'two meals' are.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
How much is its measure?
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the food of the עירוב.

phrases.english: Food for two meals
for each and every one.
phrases.notes: Each person who relies on the עירוב needs his own two-meal amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The topic moves from who is included in an עירוב to how much food it needs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב needs food for two meals for each person included in it.

steps.title: Weekday meals or שבת meals
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר measures the two meals by weekday eating. רבי יהודה measures them by שבת eating. Both are trying to be lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: We measure by a person's weekday food and not his שבת food. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: we measure by שבת food and not weekday food. Both of them mean to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about whose 'meal' sets the size. Is it a weekday meal or a שבת meal?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא picks the smaller meal, so the required amount is lower. רבי מאיר thinks people eat more on שבת, so the weekday meal is smaller. רבי יהודה thinks people eat more bread on a weekday, so the שבת meal is smaller. The argument is about facts of eating, not about wanting to be strict or lenient.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one of them is being strict. Both want the smaller amount. They only disagree about which day people eat less.

phrases.english: His food for a weekday and not for Shabbos,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
For Shabbos and not for a weekday,
and both this one and that one intend to be lenient.
phrases.notes: Each picks the day on which he thinks people eat less.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְזוֹנוֹ לַחוֹל וְלֹא לַשַּׁבָּת דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines whose meal sets the 'two meals' measure from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר measures by weekday meals and רבי יהודה by שבת meals. Each chooses the smaller amount in order to be lenient.

steps.title: Measuring two meals by a loaf of bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה and רבי שמעון each set the two-meal measure as a specific size of loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: a loaf bought for a פונדיון, at a time when four סאה of wheat sell for a סלע. רבי שמעון says: two-thirds of a loaf, when three loaves are made from a קב.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more תנאים give a concrete size for 'two meals.' Each one uses a loaf of bread as the measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה measures by price. He means a loaf bought for one פונדיון (1/48 of a סלע) when wheat costs four סאה per סלע. רבי שמעון measures by size. He means two-thirds of a loaf, where each loaf is one-third of a קב of flour. These give a fixed amount instead of depending on how much people eat.

keyTerms.meaning: A small coin worth 1/48 of a סלע
A dry measure equal to six קב

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
A loaf bought for a pundeyon,
when four se'ah of wheat sell for a sela.
phrases.notes: This fixes the price of wheat, so the loaf's size is known.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Two parts of a loaf,
phrases.notes: Two out of three parts, which is two-thirds.

phrases.english: when three loaves are made from a kav.
phrases.notes: Each loaf is one-third of a קב.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר מִכִּכָּר בְּפוּנְדְּיוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers fixed bread measures for 'two meals,' instead of measuring by eating habits as in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two meals equal a loaf bought for a פונדיון at four סאה per סלע (רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה), or two-thirds of a loaf made at three loaves per קב (רבי שמעון).

steps.title: Half and quarter of the loaf for other laws
steps.stepSummary: Half of this loaf is the measure for a בית המנוגע. A quarter of it is the measure of impure food that makes the body פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Half of it is the measure for a house with צרעת. Half of its half is the measure that makes the body פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same loaf to give two measures from other areas of הלכה. This is a side note, not part of the עירוב law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Half the loaf is a חצי פרס. Someone who stays in a בית המנוגע long enough to eat that amount makes his clothes טמא. A quarter of the loaf is the amount of impure food that, once eaten, makes a person's body פסול from eating תרומה by rabbinic law.

keyTerms.meaning: Its half, meaning half of the loaf

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the 'loaf' of the עירוב is a standard size used in many other areas of הלכה.

phrases.english: Its half is for the leprous house.
phrases.notes: How long one may stay there before his clothes become טמא.

phrases.english: And half of its half is to disqualify the body.
phrases.notes: Eating this much impure food makes the person פסול from תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the loaf from step 20 to give measures in other areas of הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half the loaf is the measure for a בית המנוגע. A quarter of it is the measure of impure food that makes the body פסול.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three ways to size the two meals: by eating habits (רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה), by price (רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה), and by flour (רבי שמעון). The same loaf also sets the measures of half and quarter for טומאה.

steps.title: How big are the two meals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much food 'two meals' actually is, according to רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And how much is food for two meals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a clarifying question. It is setting up the next move: a concrete size for the 'two meals' of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argued about which meal to use, but neither gave an actual amount. The גמרא now asks for that amount. It is not attacking anything. It only wants the missing number.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
And how much is food for two meals?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the actual size that steps 18 and 19 left undefined.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The concrete amount of food that counts as two meals.

steps.title: רב: two farmers' loaves
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says two meals equal two loaves of the kind farmers eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: two loaves of the farmers' kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer. Two meals equal two farmers' loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב uses a familiar everyday loaf as the measure. The meaning is one farmers' loaf for each meal, so two loaves cover two meals.

keyTerms.meaning: Of farmers, the kind of loaf farmers eat

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Two farmers' loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב תַּרְתֵּי רִיפָתָא אִיכָּרְיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two meals equal two farmers' loaves.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: two loaves of נהר פפא
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה gives a different size: two loaves of the kind baked in the area of נהר פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: two loaves of the kind made at נהר פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא answers the same question with a different local loaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both answers say 'two loaves,' one per meal. They differ only in which familiar loaf sets the size. Here it is the standard loaf of the נהר פפא region, not the farmers' loaf.

keyTerms.meaning: The region of the Pappa River

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Two loaves of the Pappa River region.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר תַּרְתֵּי רִיפָתָא נְהַר פַּפָּיָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 22 that differs from step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two meals equal two standard loaves of the נהר פפא region.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks whose view רבא followed
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks רב יוסף, the son of רבא, whether his father followed רבי מאיר or רבי יהודה on the size of the two meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to רב יוסף the son of רבא: Your father, whose opinion does he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a question about practical הלכה. Which side of the משנה's argument did רבא follow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי מאיר measures the two meals by weekday eating, and רבי יהודה measures them by שבת eating. Both say they want to be lenient. רב יוסף wants to know which way רבא actually ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom does he hold? Which opinion does he follow?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him
to Rav Yosef, son of Rava:
phrases.notes: Two different people share the name רב יוסף.

phrases.english: Your father, like whom does he hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After measuring the meals in loaves, the גמרא turns to which opinion in the משנה is followed in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבא rule like רבי מאיר (weekday meals) or like רבי יהודה (שבת meals)?

steps.title: רבא followed רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The son answers that רבא held like רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The son answers: his father follows רבי מאיר. That means the two meals are measured by normal weekday eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר assumes people eat more on שבת. So measuring by the smaller weekday meals is the lenient choice, because a person needs less food to make an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who measures the two meals by weekday eating

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.

steps.title: רב יוסף agrees, citing 'there is always room for sweets'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף also rules like רבי מאיר. He explains that רבי יהודה's view clashes with the popular saying that people always find room for sweets.
steps.simpleTranslation: I too hold like רבי מאיר. If the הלכה were like רבי יהודה, there would be a difficulty from what people say: there is always room for sweets.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says he agrees with רבי מאיר. He backs it up with a common saying about how people eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה thinks people eat less on שבת, so he treats the שבת measure as the lenient one. But everyone knows that when tasty food is served, people eat more. So שבת meals are bigger, and the weekday measure of רבי מאיר is the lenient and correct one.

keyTerms.meaning: As people say: a popular saying
There is always room for sweets
It is difficult; there would be a problem

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get the two opinions backwards. רבי מאיר says weekday meals, because he thinks שבת meals are larger. רבי יהודה says שבת meals, because he thinks שבת meals are smaller. Each one is trying to pick the smaller, lenient measure.

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא נָמֵי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: I too hold like Rabbi Meir.
For if it were like Rabbi Yehuda,
there would be a difficulty from what people say:
There is always room for sweets.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, קַשְׁיָא הָא דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף adds his own agreement and a reason for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר, because people eat more when delicacies are served, so שבת meals are larger.
steps.whatToRemember: Practical ruling: the two meals of an עירוב are measured by weekday eating, like רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the two measures are nearly the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's opinion of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, then a ברייתא saying his measure and רבי שמעון's are close to equal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says. A ברייתא taught: their words are close to being equal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's next opinion. It quotes a teaching that the two measures of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה and רבי שמעון are almost the same. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא gives the two-meal measure as a different-looking loaf size. The ברייתא claims that in real amounts they come out about equal.

keyTerms.meaning: Their words are close to being equal

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says.
phrases.notes: Quoting the words of the משנה.

phrases.english: It was taught: and their words are close to being equal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the measures of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה and רבי שמעון from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא says the measures of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה and רבי שמעון are almost equal.

steps.title: The numbers are far apart: four meals versus nine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. By רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's measure there are 4 meals in a קב, and by רבי שמעון's there are 9. How can that be called close?
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really alike?! According to רבי יוחנן, there are four meals to a קב. According to רבי שמעון, there are nine meals to a קב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. When you work out the math, the two measures are very different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, two meals are half a קב, so one meal is a quarter קב, which makes 4 meals per קב. For רבי שמעון, two meals are two-thirds of a loaf that is one-third of a קב, so one meal is one-ninth of a קב, which makes 9 meals per קב. That is more than double, which is hardly 'close.'

keyTerms.meaning: A קב, a unit of dry measure

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי יוחנן' means רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה from the משנה, not the אמורא רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Are they really alike?!
According to Rabbi Yochanan, four meals to a kav,
according to Rabbi Shimon, nine meals to a kav!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's claim from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the two measures are close to equal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Working out the math gives 4 meals per קב against 9 meals per קב, which is a big difference.

steps.title: רב חסדא: remove the grocer's third
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's loaf is priced at the store, and one-third of that price is the grocer's profit. So the actual amount of food is smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Take out one-third of them for the grocer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tries to shrink the gap. He points out that a store-bought loaf contains less food than its price suggests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה measured by a loaf bought for a פונדיון. Part of that price is the grocer's profit, so the real bread is only two-thirds of half a קב, which is one-third of a קב for two meals. That makes one meal one-sixth of a קב, so 6 meals per קב instead of 4.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Take out one-third of them for the grocer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: צֵא מֵהֶן שְׁלִישׁ לַחֶנְוָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the קשיא of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recalculation: the price-based measure includes the grocer's profit, which must be taken out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the whole half-קב price was bread, giving 4 meals per קב.
steps.terutzMaskana: After removing the grocer's third, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's measure is 6 meals per קב.

steps.title: Still a gap: nine versus six
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that even after רב חסדא's adjustment, it is 9 meals per קב for רבי שמעון and 6 for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. That is still not close.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, for one master it is nine, and for the other master it is six!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא's answer. His adjustment helps, but it does not close the gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא brought רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה from 4 up to 6 meals per קב. רבי שמעון is still at 9. A difference of 6 against 9 still seems too large to call 'close to equal.' The next step answers this with רב חסדא's other statement.

phrases.english: But still, according to one master, nine,
and according to the other master, six!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's answer in step 30 as not enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's adjustment as a full answer to the ברייתא's claim of near-equality.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even with the grocer's third removed, it is 6 meals per קב against 9, which is still a big gap.

steps.title: Using רב חסדא's other statement: the grocer takes half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the previous question with a different statement of רב חסדא. The grocer keeps half the price as profit, not one-third.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, explain it like the other statement of רב חסדא, who said: subtract half of the price for the grocer.
steps.whatsHappening: The one-third answer did not make the two measures close enough. So the גמרא switches to רב חסדא's other teaching, that half the price goes to the grocer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If half the store price is profit, the real food in רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's loaf is even smaller. That gives more meals per קב, about 8 instead of 6. Now the number is much closer to רבי שמעון's 9.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and offers a new one)

phrases.english: Rather, like the other (statement) of Rav Chisda,
who said: Subtract from them half for the grocer.
phrases.notes: Half of the store price is the grocer's markup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed one-third answer (Step 30), which Step 31 rejected, with a one-half answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recalculation using a different known statement of the same אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With one-third profit, it is 6 meals versus 9, which is not close.
steps.terutzMaskana: With one-half profit, it is 8 meals versus 9, which is close.

steps.title: But it is still nine against eight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes again: even with the half-profit answer, the two measures are not the same. רבי שמעון has 9 meals and רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה has 8.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still: for one Sage it is nine, and for the other Sage it is eight!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that 8 and 9 are still different numbers, so the gap has not fully closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new calculation narrowed the gap but did not erase it. The גמרא asks whether a one-meal difference is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: According to this Sage... and according to that Sage

phrases.english: But still: according to one Sage, nine,
and according to the other Sage, eight!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the half-profit answer of Step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the two measures are 'close to equal'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 8 is not 9, so the measures are still not equal.

steps.title: That is exactly what 'close' means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא never said the measures were equal. It said they were close, and 8 versus 9 is close.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what it means when it says, 'And their words are close to being equal.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last question by rereading the ברייתא's exact words. It only said 'close to equal', not 'equal'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'close to being equal' already admits a small difference. A one-meal gap fits that description. A gap of 4 or 6 against 9 did not.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what it means when it says

steps.whatToRemember: With the grocer taking half, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה comes to 8 meals per קב and רבי שמעון to 9. That is why the ברייתא calls them 'close to equal'.

phrases.english: That is what it means when it says:
'And their words are close to being equal.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 33 by reading the ברייתא's wording precisely.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the source's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא claims the measures are fully equal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only claims they are close, and 8 versus 9 qualifies.

steps.title: רב חסדא contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רב חסדא gave two different numbers for the grocer's profit: one-third and one-half.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between רב חסדא and רב חסדא!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the גמרא has used both of רב חסדא's statements, it notices they conflict. Which is it, a third or a half?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same אמורא cannot hold two different profit rates unless the cases are different. The גמרא is asking for the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a contradiction between... and...

phrases.english: There is a contradiction between Rav Chisda and Rav Chisda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the two statements used in Steps 30 and 32 against each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's two statements about the grocer's profit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One statement says one-third and the other says one-half. Both cannot be right as a single rule.

steps.title: It depends on who supplies the firewood
steps.stepSummary: There is no contradiction. When the homeowner supplies the wood, the grocer takes one-third. When the grocer supplies the wood himself, he takes one-half.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This case is where the homeowner provides the wood; that case is where the homeowner does not provide the wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by splitting the two statements into two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the homeowner brings the wood, the grocer only charges for his work, so one-third. If the grocer pays for the wood too, he charges more, so one-half. Both of רב חסדא's numbers are correct, each in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces a resolution)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא — דְּקָא יָהֵיב בַּעַל הַבַּיִת צִיבֵי.
phrases.english: This is where the homeowner provides the wood,

phrases.aramaic: הָא — דְּלָא יָהֵיב בַּעַל הַבַּיִת צִיבֵי.
phrases.english: and that is where the homeowner does not provide the wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא דְּקָא יָהֵיב בַּעַל הַבַּיִת צִיבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 35.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא's two profit figures contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: One-third applies when the homeowner supplies the wood, and one-half when he does not.

steps.title: The משנה's next phrase: half a loaf and a quarter loaf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה. Half the loaf is the measure for a בית המנוגע, and a quarter of the loaf is the measure for פסול הגויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Half of it is for the leprous house, and half of its half is for disqualifying the body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes with the loaf's size and quotes the next line of the משנה, setting up a discussion of these measures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the עירוב loaf as a ruler for other הלכות. Eating half a loaf is the time it takes for clothes to become טמא in a בית המנוגע. Eating a quarter loaf of טמא food makes a person פסול from eating תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of its half, a quarter loaf
To disqualify the body from eating תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: The half-loaf for a בית המנוגע is a measure of TIME (how long it takes to eat it), not an amount one must eat.

phrases.english: Half of it is for the leprous house,
and half of its half is to disqualify the body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the loaf's size and quotes the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half the עירוב loaf measures the time for a בית המנוגע. A quarter of it is the amount of טמא food that makes the body פסול from eating תרומה.
